sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) interview questions cover the platform powering an increasing share of Java backend roles — the core GCP services for backend developers (Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud SQL, Spanner, BigQuery), Pub/Sub messaging, Cloud Storage, IAM and Workload Identity, Secret Manager, Cloud Monitoring, and the deployment patterns for Spring Boot on Cloud Run vs GKE. Use this page when the job description specifies GCP — the questions are different enough from AWS that a generic cloud answer will not cut it.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
GCP = **opinionated, managed-first** Google Cloud.

- **Compute** — Cloud Run < GKE < GCE.
- **Data** — Cloud SQL (relational), Spanner (global SQL), BigQuery (analytics), Firestore (KV/doc).
- **Messaging** — Pub/Sub for everything async.
- **IAM** — workload identity > service-account keys.
- **Operations** — Cloud Monitoring + Logging + Trace, all integrated.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Gcp compute and deployment** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gcp core services** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gcp messaging** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gcp observability** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gcp security and iam** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gcp storage and data** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Cloud Run autoscales to zero** — cheap, but cold starts.
- **Spanner** is the only globally-consistent SQL — at a price.
- **Workload identity** — no static keys for GKE workloads.
- **Service-account JSON keys** are the security smell — rotate or eliminate.
- **BigQuery on-demand vs flat-rate** — pick by predictability of spend.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For Spring Boot on GCP I'd ship Cloud Run with a min-instance for warmth, use Cloud SQL for transactional data, BigQuery for analytics, secrets in Secret Manager, identity via Workload Identity, and observability via Cloud Operations."*
